slides.heading: Get it checked if you notice
items: Pain that wakes you at night

caption:
Mr Turtle bought a standing desk and his back still grumbles. Standing desks are genuinely handy because they make it easy to change position. On their own, though, they're not a solution for back or neck pain.

Stand still all day and the feet, legs and lower back start to ache instead. That's one static posture swapped for another. The goal is variety: sit, stand, walk and move.

Hybi's setup: desk at about elbow height, screen at eye level, a soft mat or supportive shoes. Switch every 30 to 45 minutes, stand for calls, sit for focused work, and take a short walk every hour. Regular activity outside work tends to matter more than any piece of furniture. Book online via the link in bio 🐢

General information only — not a substitute for an individual assessment.
